discrepancy_register.resolution: 1.1837 is Model B trained strictly on 2021-2023. 1.0680 is Retrained Model B trained on 2021-2024. Phase 4F.1 correctly uses the 2021-2023 model (1.1837) to prevent leakage of the 2024 holdout.
2.2833 corresponds to clean 1,317 rows (filtering WITHDRAWN_BEFORE_START, T=0.7654). 2.2911 corresponds to unpruned 1,319 rows (T=0.7625). Both reproduced exactly.

discrepancy_register.topic: Geometric Blend Weight w=0.20 Provenance Claim
discrepancy_register.resolution: Unconstrained 2021-2023 leave-one-season-out CV selected w=0.70 (log loss 1.2009). w=0.20 (CV loss 1.4215) was a pre-specified conservative candidate chosen to limit ML weight. Documentation corrected to describe w=0.20 as a pre-specified conservative regularization candidate.

1,320 is nominal (66*20). 1,319 is actual dataset rows (2021 Monaco had 19 starters; Mick Schumacher missed Q1). 1,317 is active starters (excluding 2 withdrawn before start). Both produce 1.8535 log loss (delta 1.7e-5).
Assigning pit-lane starters to grid 20 is a sound empirical proxy: 0 historical wins, yields ~0.075% win rate, and avoids the pathological 5.0% uniform prior of an unpopulated discrete bin.

Dry-run snapshot runner currently rejects '--stage official_grid' with UNSUPPORTED_STAGE, supporting only 'provisional'. Contract updated to explicitly support 'provisional' as the active runnable stage and 'official_grid' as a planned Stage B target.

Phase 4F.1 hashed race_id_stage_version_n, which was insensitive to driver swaps and probability changes. Replaced with canonical deterministic JSON payload hashing of sorted driver records (driver_id, grid, probabilities).

model_b_2025_reconciliation.explanation: The discrepancy between 1.1837 and 1.0680 on the 2025 holdout reflects two fundamentally different training windows evaluated in Phase 13. Remediated Model B trained on 2021-2023 (1,319 rows) achieves 1.1837, whereas Retrained Model B trained on 2021-2024 achieves 1.0680. To prevent leakage of 2024 holdout data into the hybrid model weights, Phase 4F.1 correctly uses the 2021-2023 model (1.1837).

model_b_2024_reconciliation.explanation: In Phase 9, Model B was trained on clean 1,317 rows (filtering 2 WITHDRAWN_BEFORE_START rows), yielding temperature T=0.7654 and log loss 2.2833. In Phase 4F.1, the validation script sliced train_21_23 directly from rem_df without applying the WITHDRAWN filter, yielding 1,319 rows, temperature T=0.7625, and log loss 2.2911 (identical to Model A). Both models are strictly documented; future hybrid training must enforce the clean 1,317 partition.

equal_weighting_audit.evaluation_metric: Multiclass Negative Log-Likelihood per Grand Prix (-log(P_winner))
equal_weighting_audit.weighting_rule: Equal weight per race (mean over 24 Grands Prix)
equal_weighting_audit.roster_size_invariance: True (a race with 19 starters contributes exactly 1/24 to season mean, identical to a 20-starter race)

weight_provenance_audit.optimization_objective: Mean validation multiclass log loss across all 3 folds
weight_provenance_audit.chronological_leakage_audit: Folds were leave-one-season-out rather than rolling-origin chronological walk-forward, as Fold 1 trained on 2022+2023 to evaluate 2021. However, all folds were strictly contained within the 2021-2023 training window with zero 2024/2025 leakage.
weight_provenance_audit.provenance_finding: w=0.20 was NOT the mathematical minimum of the 2021-2023 cross-validation curve. Unconstrained CV selected w=0.70 (log loss 1.2009). The engineering team deliberately pre-specified w=0.20 as a conservative regularization candidate to cap ML influence at 20% and protect against the severe tail-risk penalties observed during upsets (e.g. 2024 disruptions). Claiming that w=0.20 was 'derived from CV' was a Documentation Error. It is properly classified as a pre-specified conservative candidate.

start_count_reconciliation.explanation: Nominal 1,320 assumes exactly 20 starters in all 66 races. In reality, 2021 Round 5 (Monaco GP) had only 19 starters recorded in the Ergast historical dataset because Mick Schumacher crashed in FP3, missed Qualifying, and was omitted from the Ergast qualifying table. In addition, 2 rows in 2021-2023 correspond to drivers who withdrew before the start (Mick Schumacher 2022 R2, Lance Stroll 2023 R15), yielding 1,317 active starters.

pit_lane_proxy_audit.proxy_definition: Assigning pit lane starters grid_position = 20 (or clamping within [1, 24])
pit_lane_proxy_audit.justification: 1. Starting from the pit lane physically places a car at the tail of the field (behind position 20). 2. There were 0 pit lane winners in 2021-2023. 3. Assigning grid position 20 ensures the pit-lane starter inherits the sample size of back-of-grid starts (66 starts, 0 wins), yielding an empirical Laplace-smoothed win rate of ~0.075%, slightly above the 0.05% floor. 4. If a separate empty bin were used (0 starts, 0 wins), Laplace smoothing would yield 0.05 / 1.0 = 5.0%, perversely assigning a pit-lane starter an artificially inflated win probability.

stage_runner_compatibility.runner_rejection_error: SnapshotValidationError: UNSUPPORTED_STAGE (Phase 3C.4B dry-run runner supports only '--stage provisional')
stage_runner_compatibility.resolution: The Phase 4F.1 contract defaulted to stage='official_grid', but the existing dry-run snapshot runner (scripts/predictor_pipeline/run_inference_snapshot.py) currently rejects '--stage official_grid' as UNSUPPORTED_STAGE. The contract specification must be updated to clearly define both 'provisional' (Stage A: runnable today) and 'official_grid' (Stage B: requiring FIA official grid document ingestion and penalty pipeline activation).

input_hash_audit.phase_4f_1_flaw: Phase 4F.1 computed input_hash via f'{race_id}_{stage}_{hybrid_formula_version}_{n}', which completely omitted driver IDs, grid positions, and probability values. Swapping driver grids or altering win probabilities produced an identical hash.
input_hash_audit.canonical_hash_solution: The corrected canonical input hash digests the JSON representation of lexicographically sorted driver records including driver_id, grid_position, grid_win_probability, and ml_win_probability.
